messages:
jon_corp: Hey — noticed a big discrepancy between what our dashboard shows as served tokens and what we were billed. Dashboard: ~1.2M tokens for Mar 3-4, invoice shows ~1.9M. Can someone help? sample request id: req_01FJX9ZQ
ashley_support: Sorry about that — we'll look into it. Can you paste the request id(s) and the model + deployment name? Any chance you were using continuous batching / warmup? :thinking:
jon_corp: Model: redwood-alpha-1, route: /v1/generate, deployment: prod-east-1a. We do have continuous_batching enabled on the client (sdk default). One sample request id above (req_01FJX9ZQ) — I can provide more if needed.
samir_eng: thanks @jon_corp. Quick note: continuous batching + prefix/KV cache interactions have caused confusing served vs billed numbers before. That said, 700k delta is large. Can you confirm whether you had any burst warmup jobs or a big prefix cache prefetch around that window?
jon_corp: we did run a warmup job the night of Mar 3 to reduce cold starts. It hit ~50k synthetic requests over 30m. should that explain 700k?
maria_finance: tagging finance here — invoice id INV-2026-0312 is the one with the spike. we'll need logs correlating billing events to requests.
ashley_support: jon, pls send 3 things:
1) a couple of concrete request ids (like you gave)
2) your client config (continuous_batching true/false, batch_window_ms)
3) approximate times for the warmup job
jon_corp: here — client config snippet:
```
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
client.continuous_batching = True
client.batch_window_ms = 30
```
warmup window: 2026-03-03T02:15:00Z -> 2026-03-03T02:45:00Z
samir_eng: good — that's a very small batch_window_ms but continuous batching will keep an open batching goroutine that occasionally prefetches KV for upcoming sequences. What likely happened:
- Warmup created many short prefix requests that miss the cache initially.
- The runtime's prefetch/continuous-batching paths may send extra tokens upstream as part of batch aggregation and KV prefetch peers.
- Our served-tokens metric excludes internal prefetch responses that are never returned to the customer, but invoices historically counted total token work for the host process (including prefetch & batching overhead) in edge cases. We're working to make this consistent but older meters can show "billed > served".
ashley_support: @samir_eng can you confirm whether an internal prereq/replica warmup caused the extra billed tokens for req_01FJX9ZQ? infrabot, can you pull the runtime traces for that window?
infrabot: fetched logs for prod-east-1a 2026-03-03 02:00-03:00 UTC. Relevant excerpt (condensed):
```
[02:16:12] batch_open id=BX-77 size=1 batch_window_ms=30
[02:16:12] kv_prefetch start prefix_id=pfx-9a hit=false
[02:16:12] kv_prefetch tokens_sent=128
[02:16:12] batch_dispatch id=BX-77 to_replicas=3 tokens_total=512
[02:16:12] kv_prefetch hit=true (subsequent) tokens_sent=0
[02:16:13] response to client tokens_sent=32
```
samir_eng: see that? The first request triggered a kv_prefetch that sent ~128 tokens to the model per replica (3 replicas) before the client-visible response was returned (which was 32 tokens). Billing aggregator counted tokens_total=512 for that batch dispatch. The served metric counts the client-visible 32. That matches a scenario where billed >> served.
jon_corp: so billed includes the internal replica prefetch across all replicas? that seems surprising.
samir_eng: historically yes in edge cases — we bill for model work across replicas and prefetch work when it can't be attributed as a pure cache hit. If prefetch later hits the cache for subsequent requests, those subsequent requests show low served tokens.
maria_finance: for invoicing we're seeing aggregated token-work from the runtime metrics stream. If you'd like, we can audit by request id to produce an itemized breakdown (this may take 24-48h). Do you want us to start that audit now, @jon_corp?
jon_corp: please do. We need a breakdown to present to our finance team. Also, is there any mitigation to avoid this in future? We didn't expect warmups to increase our bill by that much.
ashley_support: mitigation options:
- Increase batch_window_ms so prefetches are batched with real traffic less often (reduces unnecessary replica prefetch per short bursts).
- Disable continuous_batching during synthetic warmups.
- Use the warmup API mode (we have a non-billed warmup path for customers on enterprise/Reserved) — I'll check your account tier.
samir_eng: short-term patch: mark warmup requests with header `X-Redwood-Warmup: true` and we'll exclude them from billing attribution after manual review. Long-term: we're updating invoicing to not count intra-replica prefetch once it's attributed to a subsequent cache hit (ETA 2 weeks).
jon_corp: thanks. I'll ask my infra team to tag warmup requests and send the additional request ids.
maria_finance: starting audit for INV-2026-0312 now. We'll DM you privately with preliminary findings and a timeline. If the audit shows an unexpected attribution, we'll issue an adjustment.
ashley_support: noted — assigning case #SUP-2026-489. Will follow up as we get results. :thumbsup:
jon_corp: appreciated. Quick Q — any recommended snippets to tag warmup requests? example?
samir_eng: add header + use small payloads. Example curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Warmup: true" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"warmup short prompt"}'
```
jon_corp: perfect. I'll roll that out and follow up with the extra ids. Thanks all.
